title: Vanishing of first cohomology for ideal twists implies ampleness
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Suppose that for every quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ [pqf-def-coherent] there exists an integer $n\ge1$ such that $H^1(X,\mathcal I\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal L^{\otimes n})=0$, with cohomology as in [pqf-def-cohomology] and tensor product and powers as in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Then $\mathcal L$ is ample in the absolute sense of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module].

proof.text: Since f is proper and Spec(R) is affine, the proper-basic lemma makes X quasi-compact. We will construct affine nonvanishing neighbourhoods for every closed point, then show that their union is X.

source.place: Tag 0B5U, lemma-vanshing-gives-ample (3) => (1), and Tag 0B5P, lemma-quasi-compact-h1-zero-invertible, hypothesis (1).

proof.text: Fix a point x whose singleton is closed in X. Apply the common-free-generator lemma with M=N=L and W=X to choose an affine open U containing x and a generator e of L on U. Put Z=X minus U and Z' = Z union {x}. The reduced-induced-closed-subscheme lemma gives quasi-coherent ideal sheaves I=I_Z and J=I_{Z'}. Its explicit vanishing-ideal formula gives J contained in I, I restricted to U equal to O_U, and I restricted to X minus {x} equal to J restricted there. At x the inclusion J_x into I_x=O_{X,x} has image m_x, because vanishing at x means having zero image in its residue field. Both Z and Z' are closed; in particular J is among the ideal sheaves quantified in the hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0B5P, proof, choice of x,U,Z,Z' and reduced ideals; Schemes lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme (Tag 01J3).

proof.text: In the abelian category of module sheaves put Q=I/J, the sheafification of the sectionwise quotient. The inclusion and its cokernel give 0 -> J -> I -> Q -> 0. For each n>=1 put M_n=L^{tensor n}. Tensoring this sequence by M_n gives 0 -> J tensor M_n -> I tensor M_n -> Q tensor M_n -> 0, and I tensor M_n -> M_n is injective. Here is the local verification, so no flatness assertion is implicit: on any open V where M_n has generator a, each map F tensor M_n -> F is f tensor (r a) |-> r f, with inverse f |-> f tensor a. Under these identifications both the sequence and the inclusion into M_n are the original exact sequence and I -> O_X. These identifications commute with every map in the sequence. Exactness follows locally on this covering: kernels are sectionwise, and cokernels are sheafified sectionwise cokernels. Such a cover exists because powers of an invertible module are invertible.

source.place: Tag 0B5P, proof, the two displayed short exact sequences; the tensor sequence is checked in local generators.

proof.text: Choose n>=1 with H^1(X,J tensor M_n)=0, using the hypothesis for the quasi-coherent ideal J, and write M=M_n. Construct q_n in Gamma(X,Q tensor M) explicitly on the open cover {U, X minus {x}}. On U use the image of e^{tensor n} under M|_U=(I tensor M)|_U -> (Q tensor M)|_U, using I|_U=O_U. On X minus {x} use zero: there I=J, hence Q=0 and Q tensor M=0. The two sections agree on U minus {x}, since this quotient sheaf is zero there, and therefore glue by the sheaf axiom. At x their germ is the class of e^{tensor n} modulo m_x M_x. In its generator coordinate this class is 1 in kappa(x), which is nonzero.

source.place: Tag 0B5P, proof, choice of n and the residue-one quotient section. Gluing on U and X minus {x} expands the source's identification of global quotient sections with A/m.

proof.text: The category of O_X-module sheaves is abelian with enough injectives. Global sections is additive and left exact: an element lies in the sectionwise kernel exactly when its image is zero. Apply the right-derived universal delta-functor lemma to Gamma(X,-) and the short exact sequence of step 3 at the selected n. Its R^0 Gamma = Gamma identification and exactness give Gamma(X,I tensor M) -> Gamma(X,Q tensor M) -> H^1(X,J tensor M). The last group is zero by the chosen n, so the boundary of q_n is zero; exactness gives t in Gamma(X,I tensor M) mapping to q_n. Denote by s its image in Gamma(X,M) under the inclusion I tensor M -> M. This uses only H^1 vanishing for J at this one n, not eventual vanishing or vanishing for I.

source.place: Tag 0B5P, proof, existence of the global lift s from the chosen H^1 vanishing; Cohomology of Sheaves, cohomology long exact sequence.

proof.text: The value of s at x is the nonzero class of e^{tensor n}, so x belongs to X_s. At any z in Z, trivialize M on a neighbourhood with generator a. Since s comes from I tensor M, its coordinate in this generator is a section of I, and the vanishing-ideal formula makes its residue at z zero. Thus s has zero value at every z in Z and X_s is contained in U. On U write s=f e^{tensor n}, with f in O_X(U). The definition of X_s says that for y in U, y belongs to X_s exactly when f has nonzero residue at y, equivalently its germ is a unit in the local ring O_{X,y}. Consequently X_s=U_f. The affine-principal-open lemma (0) says that U_f is affine. This completes the construction for every closed point x.

source.place: Tag 0B5P, proof, x in X_s contained in U and X_s=D(f) affine.

proof.text: Let W be the union of X_s over all positive powers and sections whose nonvanishing open is affine. Each X_s is open by the ampleness-definition node, and steps 2--6 show that W contains every closed point. The underlying space of X is Kolmogorov: if two points had the same closure, that irreducible closed subset would have two generic points, contrary to the scheme-sobriety lemma; distinct closures are distinguished by an open complement. Apply the quasi-compact Kolmogorov closed-point lemma to the closed subset X minus W of the quasi-compact space X. If nonempty, it contains a point closed in X, contradicting that all closed points lie in W. Hence W=X.

source.place: Tag 0B5P, final paragraph, the closed-point covering argument; the cited closed-point lemma applies directly to a closed subset of X.

proof.text: X is quasi-compact by step 1. The equality W=X gives, for every point of X, a positive power of L and a section of that power with affine nonvanishing locus containing the point. These are precisely the two clauses of absolute ampleness. Therefore L is ample.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0B5U, lemma-vanshing-gives-ample (3) => (1), expanded by the full proof of Tag 0B5P, lemma-quasi-compact-h1-zero-invertible.
